correctness.rationale: The unit transform is one-to-one and parameter-independent, so it preserves the score and Fisher information. Twice differentiating the exact parent Shanker log density leaves one non-elementary expectation, which evaluates to \(\alpha^2 e^{\alpha^2}E_1(\alpha^2)/(\alpha^2+1)\). The endpoint asymptotics of \(E_1\) prove that \(\alpha\sqrt{I(\alpha)}\) has different limits at zero and infinity, decisively excluding proportionality to \(1/\alpha\). The separate posterior-propriety statement follows from exact endpoint powers and exponential decay.

value.rationale: The target paper reports Bayesian posterior plots, point estimates, credible intervals, and simulation comparisons under what it labels a Jeffreys prior. The exact prior derived here shows that those reported columns correspond instead to a log-uniform prior. Because changing the prior changes the posterior and its summaries, correct Jeffreys-prior results require recomputation. At the same time, proving propriety of the published log-uniform posterior prevents overstatement: the existing numerical analysis is meaningful under a different prior rather than mathematically undefined.
